nodes.text: P1 resolved: Transaction TXN-C02-DISPUTED is at Merchant MER-C02 (Bluefern Coffee Roasters). Descriptor DSC-C02-TAPR ('TAPR* BLUEFERN CAFE BOSTON') describes the transaction and is SUB_MERCHANT_OF MER-C02, so the descriptor identifies the Bluefern sub-merchant/business under its acquiring/payment-facilitator descriptor prefix TAPR; it is not evidence that TAPR is the merchant itself. The historical descriptor DSC-C02-OLD ('BLUEFERN COFFEE ROASTERS') directly describes MER-C02, corroborating the underlying merchant identity.

No REFUNDS, reversal transaction, FOR_ORDER/linked order, RELATED_TO, or CLEARS/authorization edge is attached to the target; therefore no identified lifecycle relationship changes the amount at issue. The only transaction associations are payment with CRD-C02, merchant MER-C02, descriptor DSC-C02-TAPR, and dispute DSP-2026-90002. nodes.text: CUS-C02 has two prior, undisputed card-present purchases at Bluefern Coffee Roasters on the same card before the disputed charge: TXN-C02-PRIOR-A (2026-08-04, $9.75) and TXN-C02-PRIOR-B (2026-08-27, $12.60), both on CRD-C02 and MER-C02. The disputed TXN-C02-DISPUTED is the same card and merchant; only the billing descriptor changed from BLUEFERN COFFEE ROASTERS (DSC-C02-OLD) to TAPR* BLUEFERN CAFE BOSTON (DSC-C02-TAPR), with the latter linked as a sub-merchant descriptor. No terminal, device, token, IP, or SAME_ACTOR/COMPROMISED_AT relationship is present for CUS-C02 in the queried history, so the graph supports prior recognition/repeated use and not a common-actor compromise pattern.

The graph nevertheless resolves the substantive points: TAPR* BLUEFERN CAFE BOSTON maps to Bluefern Coffee Roasters, with two prior undisputed purchases on the same card; the transaction is labeled card_present but physical presentment is not independently corroborated. nodes.text: P6 assessment: No broader compromise pattern is modeled for the C02 case. CRD-C02/ACC-C02/CUS-C02 and MER-C02 show three repeated card-present purchases (two undisputed prior purchases and the disputed purchase), but the target has no modeled terminal, device, token, IP, authorization/clearing, or SAME_ACTOR/COMPROMISED_AT link. MER-C02 has only this one disputed transaction. A separate dense C11 fraud cluster exists on DEV-C11-NEW/IP-C11-VPN, but no identifier path connects it to C02.

nodes.label: MemoryNote
nodes.text: When authorization, clearing, terminal, POS, token, or device records are absent from the graph and no linked EvidenceRequest shows that a party failed to provide them, classify presentment/authorization as uncorroborated or unavailable—not as affirmative fraud evidence and not as an unanswered-request default. Obtain external issuer/acquirer records when physical presentment is outcome-determinative.

nodes.label: MemoryNote
nodes.text: When a statement descriptor contains a facilitator/processor prefix plus a recognizable business name, resolve it against graph relationships before treating it as a separate merchant. A descriptor linked to the transaction and modeled as SUB_MERCHANT_OF the underlying merchant, especially when a historical descriptor directly describes that merchant, supports descriptor alias/facilitator confusion rather than unrelated-merchant fraud. This pattern is reusable, but external acquiring records may still be needed to identify the facilitator legally.

nodes.label: MemoryNote
nodes.text: Repeated undisputed use of the same payment card at the same underlying merchant before a disputed charge is strong evidence of prior merchant recognition or repeated use and can outweigh an unfamiliar descriptor as an explanation. It does not by itself prove who physically presented the card, establish authorization, or rule out later unauthorized use; keep presentment and compromise questions separate.
